data.narrative:
Varda Space Industries, a Series C-stage space and aerospace company founded by Will Bruey and Delian Asparouhov, is valued at $1.5B post-money on $131M total raised. The valuation analysis draws from a comp universe of 5 public-market peers (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private-stage companies in space and aerospace, including Sierra Space, Skyryse, and others at Series B through Series D.

Two quantitative methods are applicable. Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical of Series C advancement to the last post-money valuation of $1.5B, implying $2.5B. Peer-median valuation across 5 same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables yields $2.0B; the peer range spans $1.1B (Skyryse, Series C) to $8.0B (Sierra Space, Series C). Public-comp anchoring via P/S multiples cannot be applied without disclosed revenue figures, which private companies typically do not publish.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $1.7B to $2.9B, with a median of $2.3B. This reflects the $1.5B current valuation at the lower bound of reasonableness. Key uncertainties center on revenue trajectory and the wide dispersion in Series C peer valuations (1.1x to 8.0x), which signals material stage-of-maturity and technology-risk heterogeneity within the space sector.
